caused by humans on earth. If we make least use of energy, the earth

energy. Turning them off saves money too!
So, you can tackle climate change and live comfortably. There is plenty you
can do. If we all work sensibly, we can save our lovely planet.

Helen Keller was a great humanitarian. She cared deeply for the sick. Injured and
disabled people. The disabled people have physical or mental problems that limit their
activities or senses. Helen devoted her life to help them.
Helen was born in 1880 in Alabama, USA. Her parents were Captain Arthur Keller and
Katherine Adams Keller. Her family was not rich. Their main source of income was
cotton plantation.
Helen was born healthy, but in 1882 she became deaf, dumb and blind after a high
fever. Her father heard about Perkins School for the Blind in Boston and contacted the
Director there. In 1887, the Director sent one of his best students, Anne Sullivan, to
help Helen. Anne worked hard to enable her to communicate.
In 1890, Helen's formal education started at Horace Mann School for the deaf in
Boston. In 1892, she went to Wright Humason School for the deaf in New York. Helen
improved her communication skills and studied regular academic subjects. She then
decided to go to college, and attended Cambridge School for Young Ladies in 1896.
Later, she studied at Radcliffe College. Here she learnt Braille, which was a new
technique for reading. She also learnt how to type. Anne Sullivan was always with
Helen. She sat with Helen in class and helped her by interpreting lectures and texts. In
1904, Helen received her BA degree with Honours from Radcliffe College.
Helen spent her life helping disabled people to leai.11. She died on June 1, 1968.

11. The Greedy Farmer’s Lesson
In a small village, there lived a greedy farmer named Alam. He had plenty of land and
cattle, but he always wanted more. One day, a wise old man told him about a magical
offer. "If you run from sunrise to sunset, all the land you cover will be yours," he said.
Alam, driven by greed, decided to take the challenge. The next morning, he started
running as fast as he could, marking the land he covered. By midday, he was exhausted

subject: English
text:
but continued running, thinking of the wealth he would gain. As the sun began to set,
Alam collapsed from exhaustion, realizing he had covered far more land than he could
ever manage. The wise old man appeared and said, "Greed leads to destruction. Be
content with what you have." Alam learned his lesson and returned to his village, shar-
ing his newfound wisdom with others.

subject: English
text: 12. Patriotism

subject: English
text:
Patriotism is the love and devotion for one’s country. It inspires individuals to work for
the betterment of their nation and uphold its values. A true patriot respects the country’s
history, culture, and traditions while striving to contribute to its progress. Patriotism is
not just about celebrating national holidays or waving flags; it is about taking responsi-
bility for the nation’s welfare. Patriots are willing to make sacrifices for their country,
whether by serving in the military, participating in community service, or simply being
responsible citizens. Patriotism fosters unity and strengthens the bond among people,

subject: English
text:
regardless of their differences. It encourages us to protect our country’s sovereignty
and work towards peace and prosperity. In times of crisis, patriots stand together to
overcome challenges. True patriotism is selfless and rooted in a genuine desire to see
the nation thrive. It is a virtue that every citizen should cherish and practice.
